 Football
 Soccer-Former Arsenal forward Pennant saved by his dog after German Shepherd attack
 Monday, 26 Oct 2026
 | 8:02 PM MYT
 share 
 bookmark 
 FILE PHOTO: Soccer Football - Legends of the North - Manchester United Legends v Liverpool Legends - Old Trafford, Manchester, Britain - May 21, 2022 Liverpool Legends' Jermaine Pennant during the warm up before the match Action Images via Reuters/Ed Sykes/File Photo 
 (Fixes formatting in ⁠paragraph 1)
 Oct 26 (Reuters) - Former Arsenal ⁠and Liverpool winger Jermaine Pennant was ‌saved by his own dog after a German Shepherd dog attacked him in the street, British ​media reported.
 Pennant needed more ⁠than 50 stitches ⁠after the incident and the 43-year-old posted ⁠a photo ‌on social media showing his right leg heavily bandaged.
 "So ⁠I was attacked by a German ​Shepherd, I ‌tried to protect (my dog) King but ⁠the dog ​got my leg," Pennant, who retired in 2018, wrote on Instagram.
 "I was on ⁠the floor with the dog ​still attached with no sign of letting go, until King intervened ... he fought ⁠the dog off and saved what could’ve been a horrendous situation for me."
 King suffered a minor leg injury.
 "My hero, ​still protecting me and ⁠trying to look after me, King you’re ​a legend love you, ‌man’s best friend," Pennant ​wrote.
 (Reporting by Chiranjit Ojha in Purulia, India, editing by Ed Osmond)
